CIA AND U.S. INTELLIGENCE CHIEF'S OFFICE HIT BY CYBERSECURITY BREACH — NYT

The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a cyberattack that exposed unclassified intelligence information, according to The New York Times, citing U.S. officials.

The breach reportedly affected an open-source intelligence analysis system, with information from other federal agencies potentially compromised.

Officials say classified information was not exposed, while the identity of the attackers remains unknown.

The incident follows reported breaches involving the FBI and USDA, raising concerns about cybersecurity across U.S. government systems.
(@WalterBloomberg)

CITADEL SECURITIES SMASHES ANNUAL REVENUE RECORD IN JUST NINE MONTHS

Citadel Securities generated more than $15 billion in net trading revenue during the first nine months of 2026, already surpassing its full-year 2025 record, according to Bloomberg.

Third-quarter revenue jumped 29% to over $3.4 billion, while net income rose 13% to approximately $1.19 billion.

The firm, which handles more than one-third of U.S. retail stock trades, is expanding aggressively into institutional trading, corporate bonds and equity block trades.

The results underscore Citadel Securities' growing dominance across Wall Street trading markets.
(@WalterBloomberg)

NEW YORK PROPOSES 10% TAX ON PREDICTION MARKETS — POLITICO

New York State Senator Jeremy Cooney has proposed a 10% tax on prediction market operators' net trading fee revenue to help fund universal pre-K.

Multiple city council member have come out in support of the bill which would regulate regulate prediction markets, ban elected officials and policy advisers from trading, and introduce consumer safeguards.

Cooney wants regulation and taxation rather than an outright ban.
(@WalterBloomberg)

U.S. MANUFACTURING RETURNS TO EXPANSION AS RICHMOND FED INDEX RISES TO +3

The Richmond Fed Manufacturing Composite Index climbed to +3 in November, up from -2 in October, signaling a return to modest expansion in regional factory activity.

New orders rebounded to +2 from -8, while shipments improved to +2 from 0.

Employment strengthened to +6 from +3, and capacity utilization recovered to 0 from -7.

However, price pressures remain elevated, with the prices-paid measure rising to 7.59% annualized, compared with 7.12% in October.

The report signals improving manufacturing activity alongside persistent inflation pressures.
(@WalterBloomberg)
